messages:
nina: Seeing a persistent p95 tail (~20-30ms) for short LLM RPCs on a few GPU hosts in rack r72 since ~02:40 UTC. Not a batch job. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/egress/r72

infra-bot: [Alert] egress-p95-elevated on r72 (02:42 UTC). Suggested runbook: https://confluence.internal/runbooks/egress-noise

oscar: Any obvious noisy tenant? can you run a quick attribution to top-sender cgroup/pid?

nina: Ran a quick probe. Top transmitter looks like tenant-204-metrics-sidecar (pid 7182). Host dump:
```
r72-node5:
  tx_queue_len: 44
  p95_rtt_ms: 24.7
  interrupts_pps: 108k
  softirq_skew: cpu1
  top_sender: tenant-204-metrics-sidecar:9200 (pid 7182)
```

leila: Sounds like high-pps telemetry sidecar + NAPI/coalesce issues. Four options, ordered low->high friction: 1) spread IRQ affinity across CPUs, 2) per-tenant egress policing (tc qdisc/classify by cgroup), 3) micro-proxy pool (pin a small L7 proxy pool to hosts for that tenant), 4) full dedicated GPU slice carveout. Micro-proxy is interesting as a middle-ground.

ben: Micro-proxy = reserve extra L7 workers, cheaper than GPU reservation but still adds host slots. Can finance put rough multipliers on micro-proxy vs dedicated slice? need to communicate to support.

finance: Quick posture numbers: micro-proxy pool (4 reserved proxy workers pinned) ~1.15x marginal cost for that tenant at peak (proxy CPU + small host reservation). Tiny dedicated GPU slice (single-GPU reserved with replication) ~2.6x marginal cost due to reservation headroom + replica copies + network carve. Exact depends on region and slice size.

oscar: For immediate relief let's try low-risk infra knobs first: irq spread then per-tenant policing if p95 still >5ms. If it keeps recurring or interferes with GPU streaming we'll discuss micro-proxy.

nina: I'll apply irq-affinity spread and watch 10m. If that doesn't normalize, we'll add a cgroup tc throttle.

infra-bot: Action queued: apply-irq-affinity-spread to r72-node[4-6] (02:50 UTC).

nina: IRQ spread applied. After 5m p95 -> 7.1ms (from 24.7), tx_queue_len -> 19. Promising but not baseline.

leila: Next step: per-tenant policing using tc. Example command we used elsewhere:
```
# classify tenant cgroup traffic then shape
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 30
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 1gbit
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 200mbit burst 10kb
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 handle 100 cgroup
```

ben: Also add a short kernel tweak for NAPI/accept backlogs if we see socket churn. Example sysctls: `sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=1024 net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=2048`. Low risk and quick to revert.

infra-bot: Applied per-tenant egress-policing for tenant-204 on r72-node5 (02:58 UTC).

nina: After policing p95 back to 3.3ms on the affected nodes. Looks stable in 15m window. Good immediate fix.

oscar: Can we add auto-attribution to the alert pipeline so future egress-p95 alerts include top-cgroup/pid? That will speed triage and let automation soft-quarantine quickly.

leila: I'll file INFRA-7777 for auto-attribution + soft-quarantine playbook and link it to the runbook. Also will add telemetry-jitter to exporter helm values to avoid synchronized polling.

ben: Please include the micro-proxy cost appendix (finance numbers) in the ticket so support can make quick carveout vs micro-proxy decisions. If tenant latency is customer-facing, support may ask for micro-proxy while infra investigates.

finance: Will attach a short appendix to INFRA-7777. Note: micro-proxy isolates L7 contention but won't help if tenant streams heavy token throughput (NIC-level contention) 10. In that case dedicated GPU slice remains the safety valve.

nina: Summary of short play used: 1) irq-affinity spread -> 5m observe, 2) per-tenant tc policing -> observe, 3) if recurring -> micro-proxy pool trial, 4) last resort -> dedicated slice. I'll add commands + tcpdumps to INFRA-7777. Monitoring window open for 1h. :eyes:
